title: Early-Life Exposure to Clostridium leptum Causes Pulmonary Immunosuppression.
ehr_evidence: Virgin female BALB/c mice (6–8 weeks old, 18–22 g) were obtained from the Jilin University Animal Research Center and housed in a specific pathogen–free (SPF) facility; the study used murine models and biospecimens (lung tissue, mediastinal lymph nodes, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid), not electronic health records.
summary: A controlled murine study feeding infant cesarean-delivered BALB/c mice Clostridium leptum before ovalbumin sensitization showed that early-life C. leptum exposure induced a pulmonary immunosuppressive environment with increased Treg cells and attenuated OVA-induced allergic airway inflammation and asthma phenotype.
key_findings: Early-life fed-CL increased MLN CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ Treg frequency and number in cesarean-delivered mice versus vaginally delivered mice, though the between-mode difference was not statistically significant.
C. leptum + OVA exposure did not produce the typical asthma phenotype; airway resistance to methacholine was significantly reduced versus OVA alone (p < 0.05).

Total BALF cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and macrophages were significantly increased in C/-/OVA mice versus control and significantly decreased in C/CL/OVA mice versus C/-/OVA (p < 0.05).

Th1, Th2, Th9, and Th17 lymphocyte levels and their cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-9, IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-21, IL-23) were significantly higher in C/-/OVA versus control and significantly lower in C/CL/OVA versus C/-/OVA (p < 0.05).
IL-10 and TGF-β1 in BALF were significantly decreased in C/-/OVA versus control and significantly higher in C/CL/OVA versus C/-/OVA (p < 0.05).

Th22 frequency and BALF IL-22 were significantly decreased in C/-/OVA versus control, and fed-CL did not significantly affect Th22 frequency or IL-22 (no significant difference between C/-/OVA and C/CL/OVA).
captured_features: MLN CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ Treg frequency and number (flow cytometry)
Th1, Th2, Th9, Th17, Th22 cell levels
BALF and cytokine concentrations (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-9, IL-22, IL-21, IL-23, IL-17A, IL-17F, IFN-γ, IL-10, TGF-β1, IL-25, IL-33)
BALF total and differential cell counts (eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes, macrophages)
study_design: Controlled experimental animal study (murine OVA-induced asthma model)
population: Infant cesarean-delivered and vaginally delivered BALB/c mice, early-life C. leptum feeding before OVA sensitization
limitations: Murine model with limited translatability to human pediatric asthma
Small group sizes (25 mice per group) and short observation window
Findings derived from a single bacterial strain rather than whole microbiome
data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper.
